result:
I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. I checked the method first by running it on Q2, and it reproduces all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | `consumer`, 352,803,010 KRW |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 249 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | `hw`, 290,199,453 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | `u33@ex.com` |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 239 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 699,342 KRW |
| h. August → September growth | -3.9% |

The Q2 numbers only came out right after three adjustments the definitions don't mention:
- **Time zone:** the order times in the DB (`ordered_at`) are stored in UTC. I converted them to Korean time (UTC+9) before checking whether an order falls inside the quarter and which month it belongs to. Without that, Q2 gives a different top category and a 13.9% growth rate instead of 5.4%.
- **Segment names:** the same segment is written in different ways, such as `' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '` and `'SMB'`. I lowercased them and removed the extra spaces before grouping.
- **Duplicate customers:** some email addresses have more than one customer ID. For b and f, I counted each email as one customer. Counting by customer ID gives 276 for Q2 b instead of 234.

STATUS: DONE
